mechanism.name: CURRENT_STATE_OVER_HISTORY
mechanism.one_sentence: At context-assembly time, group retrieved memory items sharing a deterministically-detected state key, render the item with the latest session timestamp as 'Current state', and render the rest as an explicit, provenance-preserving 'History (superseded)' block instead of a flat undifferentiated list.
mechanism.stage: read-side only, post-retrieval, pre-render; no Mem0/host write-path or storage change
source_systems: StateMemBench/StateMemWrapper (arXiv:2608.19652) -- Resolve step, precedence rule 1 of 4 ('later supersedes earlier'), isolated from the other 3 rules and from the LLM-mediated Trace step
STALE (arXiv:2605.06527) -- problem framing only (conflict detection); its own adjudication mechanism (LLM-over-schema) is not transplanted

AAMR-internal: memory/SCHEMA.md -- the project_memory tool's own bitemporal, append-only, current-view-derived-by-replay design, already operating in this repo, offered as an existence proof of the same architectural principle at the tooling layer, not the arena/Mem0 layer

AAMR-internal: data/lab/pmlab-stale-e1/execution-v0/report.md -- n=9 empirical measurement that content/embedding similarity cannot separate a superseded fact from its replacement (mean percentile 0.9948; stale nearest-neighbor 6/9 without a metadata filter)
not_transplanted: StateMem's TurnEncoder (per-turn LLM call) or StateStore (write-path integration)
StateMem's dependency-graph Rechecker (over-propagated -12.5pp in its own paper on one subset)
StateMemWrapper's precedence rules 2-4 (standing-vs-one-off, derived-quantity recomputation, explicit-expiry) -- out of scope for V1
StateAuditor's post-hoc draft-audit direction (a distinct architectural shape, listed as Candidate 5, not selected)

target_failure.name: STALE_STATE_CONFUSION
target_failure.canonical_example: T1: user works at Microsoft. T2: user leaves Microsoft. T3: user works at Google. Question: where does the user currently work? Failure: retrieval contains all three facts; system/reader treats them symmetrically or selects a stale one.

submodes_v1_covers.A_DIRECT_SUPERSESSION: old value -> new value, same state key
submodes_v1_covers.B_NEGATION_REVOCATION: fact -> explicitly no longer true, no replacement value asserted

submodes_v1_explicitly_out_of_scope.D_MULTI_ATTRIBUTE_STATE: one entity, multiple independently-changing fields -- partially exercised only as an adversarial negative control (R4), not as its own regime with dedicated probes
submodes_v1_explicitly_out_of_scope.E_DEPENDENCY_CASCADE: change in one state invalidating derived facts -- no dependency graph in V1; flagged as a forward risk in negative regimes (over-propagation) even though not implemented
submodes_v1_explicitly_out_of_scope.F_AMBIGUOUS_UPDATE: new statement may or may not supersede the old one -- deferred; see regimes.R5_deferred

state_key_definition.why_not_B: Schema-based keys assigned via construction-time metadata (mirroring how this arena already threads metadata['timestamp']) would answer the key-matching question only for hand-authored synthetic probes, not for the transplant mechanism itself -- it would not test whether state keys can be recovered from real, uncontrolled Mem0 fact text at all. Rejected for V1 as not actually exercising the mechanism.
state_key_definition.why_not_C: LLM-assisted keying (embedding clustering or an LLM call) is more general but introduces a second confound into a test whose primary question is about deterministic precedence rendering, and adds per-item cost. Documented as a future extension only, explicitly flagged as cost/confound, not used in V1.
state_key_definition.why_not_D: Hybrid (deterministic first pass + LLM fallback on ambiguous cases) is the natural v2 once V1 measures Option A's coverage/miss rate on real corpus text -- not needed for a first mechanistic screen on hand-authored probes designed to trigger the fixed template set.
state_key_definition.runtime_no_gold_access: The key-extraction function operates only on retrieved item text (regex/keyword match, case-insensitive substring). It never sees the question, the expected answer, or any judge/gold artifact. Construction-time probe design (which facts are meant to share a key) and runtime key-matching (how the mechanism actually decides) are kept separate: the mechanism must independently rediscover the intended grouping from text alone for the mechanistic metrics (section metrics.mechanistic) to mean anything.

templates_v1.capture: status label, not a proper noun
sub-keyed by the pet's own proper name -- deliberately keeps different pets separate
sub-keyed by named language -- deliberately keeps different languages separate
sub-keyed by address type -- deliberately keeps home vs work separate despite the shared word 'address'

state_key_definition.known_fragility: Coverage-limited to 9 fixed templates; a genuine supersession phrased outside these patterns is a false negative (missed match), not a false positive. This is the honest cost of Option A and is explicitly why V1 is a mechanistic screen, not a claim of general-purpose state-key extraction.

update_rule: later session timestamp (evidence_times, already available in the existing Mem0 adapter's deep_retrieval block, the same field TEMPORAL_ANCHOR_AT_CONTEXT already reads) wins as CURRENT for a given matched key.
supersession_rule: when >=2 retrieved items share a state key, the item with the latest timestamp is rendered as current; every other item with that key is rendered in a separate History block, each annotated with its own timestamp and an explicit 'superseded' marker plus a pointer to which item superseded it (by anonymized position, not by item id, to avoid leaking retrieval-order information the reader wasn't given before).
retrieval_rule: unchanged -- identical retrieval call, identical budget, identical ranked item list as BASE. The mechanism only transforms the already-retrieved list before rendering; it does not change what is retrieved or in what order it was retrieved.

context_rendering.base: unchanged: every retrieved item rendered as '- {text}', one per line, in retrieval order (fixed_reader.py::user_message, unmodified).
context_rendering.plus_b: retrieved items are partitioned by detected state key. Items with no detected key render exactly as in BASE, interleaved in original order. Items sharing a key are pulled into two labeled blocks appended after the undetected-key items: 'Current state:' (one line per key, its latest item) and 'History (superseded):' (remaining items per key, each tagged with its own date and 'superseded by a later update').

ambiguity_handling: if two items sharing a key have the identical latest timestamp (a tie), or if the key-matching confidence is a single-template partial match on an edge phrase, the mechanism does NOT guess: both items render in the Current block unchanged (falls back to BASE-equivalent behavior for that key only), and the tie is logged as a mechanistic-metric event, not silently resolved.
failure_fallback: if state-key extraction fails to fire on any item in a probe (0 matches), +B is byte-identical to BASE for that context -- the mechanism must be inert, not harmful, when its own detection has nothing to act on.
what_it_does_not_do: does not modify Mem0 storage, extraction, or retrieval ranking
does not delete or hide any retrieved item's provenance -- every item remains in the rendered context, only its position/label changes
does not attempt cross-key dependency propagation (failure mode E)
does not resolve ambiguous updates (failure mode F) -- ambiguous cases fall back to BASE-equivalent rendering per ambiguity_handling
does not use an LLM at any point in the V1 mechanism itself
provenance_requirements: source item id (Mem0 evidence_id) retained per rendered line, exactly as already available -- not newly introduced
source session timestamp retained and displayed per rendered line
old value and new value both remain textually present in the rendered context (never deleted)
supersession relation is positional/explicit in the rendering (which block an item is in), not merely implied by order
append_only_discipline: no memory item is ever dropped from the delivered context by this mechanism (see failure_fallback and what_it_does_not_do). The destructive-overwrite alternative (Candidate 3 on the board, DETERMINISTIC_LATEST_VALID_VALUE) was considered and explicitly not selected, flagged as a major design risk per the mandatory append-only principle.

R5_deferred.note: AMBIGUOUS_UPDATE is well-specifiable without gold-aware logic (mechanistic false-supersession-rate check, not a benchmark-accuracy check) but deliberately deferred out of V1 per the explicit instruction not to assume the first test must cover every submode. Candidate for a v1.1 probe extension (+2-3 probes), not V1.

regimes.rationale: matches the explicitly-suggested 12-probe / 3-3-3-3 distribution; no deviation proposed. Distribution frozen before any probe content was checked against expected behavior.

arms_confound_flag: context token count differs slightly between BASE and +B (block headers add a small, fixed number of tokens per probe) -- tracked explicitly as a metric, not hidden.

success_gate.label: MECHANISM_B_EXPLORATORY_SUPPORTED
conditions_all_required: positive net repairs (repairs > regressions) across the 9 R1+R2+R3 probes
zero false-supersession events across the 3 R4 control probes (false_supersession_rate == 0/3)
no systematic harm on R4 (R4 accuracy under +B >= R4 accuracy under BASE)
mechanism-level trace shows the intended causal path on every repair (reader's answer text traceably uses the Current-state block, not a coincidental match)

failure_gate.label: MECHANISM_B_FAIL
conditions_any_triggers: false supersession common (>=1 of 3 R4 controls wrongly collapsed)
any regression traceable to the mechanism suppressing or relabeling information the reader needed and had access to under BASE
effect attributable only to added context/token volume rather than the current/history structuring itself (checked via the token-delta metric and per-probe trace)
implementation required a state-key rule that referenced the probe's own expected_current/expected_history fields (a host- or gold-specific oracle, not a general pattern)

replication_gate.v1_ceiling_status: EXPLORATORY_SUPPORTED at most, even on a clean PASS -- never REPLICATED_VALIDATED_TRANSPLANT
replication_gate.path_to_replication: a fresh, independently-constructed or gold-blind-selected probe set (candidate real-corpus source: LongMemEval-S's 'knowledge-update' category, 78 units in the full corpus, 0 used anywhere in this arena to date -- verified this pass) run under the same protocol, per the roadmap's existing Stage-2 pattern (docs/research/RESEARCH_ROADMAP_EVIDENCE_DRIVEN_V1.md, Stage 2 definition), before any REPLICATED_VALIDATED_TRANSPLANT status is claimed.

first_arena_run_if_later_authorized.reader: 12 probes x 2 arms x ~$0.0006/call (roadmap F9 figure) = ~$0.014

frankenstein_relevance.vs_temporal_anchor_family: PARTIALLY_OVERLAPPING -- not ORTHOGONAL. Per docs/research/CROSS_PAPER_HYPOTHESIS_MAP_2026-08-24.md's own framing, AAMR's temporal-anchor work is 'a narrower, already-in-flight instance of this broader [state/supersession] family.' Both mechanisms consume the same evidence_times metadata and both aim at delivering the right version/timing of a fact to the reader. They differ in intervention shape: TEMPORAL_ANCHOR_AT_CONTEXT uniformly annotates every item with its date and does no grouping, filtering, or precedence logic; CURRENT_STATE_OVER_HISTORY actively restructures which items appear where, based on a detected key match, and is inert when no key matches. A future BASE/+A/+B/+A+B grid (once a temporal mechanism replicates) is a genuinely open interaction question, not a redundancy that can be assumed.
frankenstein_relevance.vs_raw_provenance_family: ORTHOGONAL. Raw provenance (E3/C4) targets missing/absent detail recovery from raw session text; this mechanism targets which of several PRESENT, already-retrieved facts is current. Different failure territory (absence vs conflicting-presence); no shared code path or shared retrieved-item property.
frankenstein_relevance.vs_harmful_sibling_failure: PARTIALLY_OVERLAPPING. Both are 'reader picks the wrong item among several plausible retrieved candidates,' but the underlying confusion differs: harmful-sibling (H5, e.g. E1's 'Spirit' case) is a same-time confusion between two DIFFERENT entities that are semantically similar (Spirit Airlines vs Delta); STALE_STATE_CONFUSION is a same-entity confusion ACROSS TIME (Microsoft then, Google now). Distinguishing axis: entity-identity vs temporal-validity. A state-key match that is too loose could, in principle, misfire in an H5-adjacent way (grouping two different entities under one key) -- this is exactly what the R4 adversarial controls (CTL1/CTL2/CTL3) are designed to catch.

future_interaction_test_note_only_not_ru.A_definition: a FUTURE, independently REPLICATED temporal mechanism -- explicitly NOT the current TEMPORAL_ANCHOR_AT_CONTEXT, which has not cleared Stage-2 replication (PM-20260824-8dc62d48, PM-20260824-36f46bed) and therefore cannot stand as 'A' in this grid yet.
future_interaction_test_note_only_not_ru.B_definition: CURRENT_STATE_OVER_HISTORY, once independently validated per the replication_gate above.
future_interaction_test_note_only_not_ru.status: not scheduled, not authorized, recorded for future reference only per docs/research/RESEARCH_ROADMAP_EVIDENCE_DRIVEN_V1.md section 11's Frankenstein gate, which requires both mechanisms independently replicated before this grid may run.

unresolved_questions: V1's 12 probes contain zero dedicated historical-question probes (e.g., 'where did I used to work before my current job?') -- the mechanism's stated risk of hiding history-needed-information (section 12's negative regime) is therefore NOT directly measured by V1's metrics; historical_question_accuracy has no data to compute from in this design. A v1.1 extension should add 2-3 such probes before the success gate can be considered complete evidence rather than partial evidence.

State-key strategy (Option A, 9 fixed templates) is measured only against probes deliberately constructed to trigger those templates -- V1 cannot measure the template set's real-corpus miss rate (false negatives on genuine supersessions phrased outside the 9 patterns). This is the central open question before any real-corpus (e.g., knowledge-update category) replication.

The tie-handling rule (identical timestamps fall back to BASE-equivalent rendering) is untested by any of the 12 probes as constructed -- no probe currently has a same-timestamp collision. Could be added cheaply to a v1.1 set.

Whether Mem0's own extraction step ever merges/dedupes two temporally-distinct statements about the same key into one stored item (which would defeat this mechanism before it ever runs) is unknown -- Mem0's near-duplicate suppression (roadmap F13, CODE_VERIFIED) is documented for redundant restatements, not verified either way for genuine value changes. Worth a cheap, deterministic check (reading stored items after a real ingest of one R1 probe) before spending on the full 12-probe run.
